narrative.overview:
Signal Command makes each new lead legible as an urgent, evidence-backed sales decision rather than another dashboard row. It is a dense but calm operating environment: persistent dark navigation frames a bright analytical canvas, while restrained indigo and cyan signals guide attention without turning the interface into an alarm panel.

The visual story moves from signal queue to performance evidence, lead detail, score rationale, next action, and delivery health. The first viewport prioritizes the queue, KPIs, qualification trend, and recent leads; promotional material and infrastructure detail stay out of that decision path.
keyCharacteristics: Fixed dark command shell around a wide, light operational canvas.
Compact, explicit status language supported by icons, labels, and color.
Indigo for action and qualification; cyan for secondary evidence.
Dense ledgers and analytical cards with quiet borders and limited elevation.
Right-side drawers preserve context while exposing evidence and next actions.

rules.name: The Semantic Signal Rule
rules.body: Rose, amber, blue, green, and red are status vocabulary, not decoration. Pair every status color with an icon or label, and do not reuse it for unrelated emphasis.

rules.name: The Scan Before Read Rule
rules.body: A user should understand the lead, its class, score, urgency, and next action from the typographic hierarchy before reading supporting prose.

rules.name: The Flat-at-Rest Rule
rules.body: Routine cards and controls use tonal contrast and a hairline border. Shadows belong to queues, overlays, drawers, dialogs, and transient feedback.

dos: Do lead operational screens with the signal queue and the most decision-relevant evidence.
Do keep routine surfaces white, bordered, compact, and flat.
Do pair every status hue with words, icons, shape, or position.
Do preserve the 244px command rail, wide analytical canvas, and contextual right drawer pattern where the workflow requires them.
Do replace dense desktop tables with purpose-built mobile cards at 620px.
donts: Don't turn Indigo or semantic status colors into broad decorative backgrounds.
Don't add promotional, celebratory, or infrastructure noise ahead of the lead decision path.
Don't float every card; reserve elevation for hierarchy and overlays.
Don't use pills as a general container shape; reserve them for compact statuses and counts.
Don't hide score rationale or next-action context behind a separate disconnected screen when a drawer can preserve the operating view.
